brief: China privately asked Iran to help rein in Yemen's Houthis, following a Saudi appeal to Beijing, and energy prices relaxed today, with Shanghai crude down 13% from its weekly highs; that eased pressure on rates as the primary driver of macro vol. Combined with a "Fed Credibility Hike" that began yesterday to reverse prior insurance cuts, equities caught a relief bid, boosted by S&P rebalance-driven pro-momentum flows into AI names, with roughly $100mm of premium bought in two-week AI stock calls (INTC, MRVL, SNDK, MU). McElligott still expects Iran-aligned pressure on the Trump administration given midterm-election stakes and a cost-of-living surge, and now sees a modified US Diesel export ban as the modal outcome within weeks, risking a fresh systemic energy supply shock compounded by a Saudi pipeline closure, Houthi seizure of Perim island, Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Syzran refinery, and China rebuilding rather than draining emergency crude stocks. He argues this could escalate rates from a grinding move higher into a high-velocity VaR event, since bonds no longer hedge equities in this inflation regime, though a subsequent growth-shock scare could flip demand toward low-strike receivers. He is buying October equity downside convexity against a one-day move.
